turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, what are the chances of such an attack happening? And how do you know the Mussulmans are planning to target us?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I know the Mussulmans are planning to target us because I have received credible information from trusted sources, not because I fear them. I am not one to be swayed by fear, but I am one who will not ignore the threat to my people and my estate.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have no intention of engaging in petty threats and counter-threats with you, Sandip. My duty is to protect my people and my estate, and I will not be swayed from that duty by your provocations. I suggest you take my warning seriously and take necessary precautions to ensure the safety of your own people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, you're getting your wires crossed again. If I were to take your warning seriously, I'd have to start building a fortress around my estate, and I think that's a bit too much for your fragile ego to handle.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, I see, so now you're a guardian of my people and estate, as well? How charming, Nikhil. Do tell, what other noble duties do you plan to take on?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You're still trying to scare me with your grand tales of conspiracy, Nikhil? I'm not impressed. I've lived through worse, and my estate has stood strong for generations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I'm starting to think you're the one who's been stirring up trouble, Nikhil. My people are loyal, and my estate is secure, no thanks to your 'warnings'.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Bimala, my love, it seems our esteemed Nikhil has once again taken leave of his senses. I suppose it's flattering, in a way, that he thinks my estate is so vulnerable.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Good heavens, Nikhil, I'm starting to think you're just bored with your own life and trying to spice things up by inventing a plot against me.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I couldn't help but notice, Nikhil, that the local Mussulmans seem to be living in a state of unease, their livelihoods threatened by some unknown force. Can you tell me, what specific evidence do you have for these alleged threats?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I assure you, Sandip, that the evidence I have is not based on hearsay or speculation. I have spoken to the local authorities and witnessed the unrest among the Mussulman population myself.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I sense a great deal of conviction in your words, Nikhil. Can you enlighten me as to what you believe I can do to protect my estate and the people who rely on it?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I implore you, Sandip, to take this seriously. Do not ignore the warning signs of growing discontent among the Mussulmans, lest you face the consequences of your own complacency.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I fear you are underestimating the situation, and your dismissal of my warnings only serves to embolden those who would seek to do harm to your estate and your people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I must admit, Nikhil, that I am increasingly concerned about the stability of our estate and the well-being of our people. Perhaps it would be wise to consider the possibility that our actions may have unintended consequences.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I have been thinking about the recent changes in the estate's management, and I wonder if perhaps we have been too quick to dismiss the Mussulman workers' grievances. Could there be a way to address their concerns and prevent... unpleasantness?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I commend you, Bimala, for your willingness to consider the concerns of the Mussulman workers. Sandip, I warn you again: your refusal to listen to reason will only lead to catastrophe.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, I will not repeat myself, but I must stress that the fate of this estate and its people is at stake. Heed my warnings, lest you face the consequences of your own actions.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be deterred from my duty to protect this estate and its people, Sandip. Mark my words, your actions will be the ruin of us all.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, I fear that Nikhil's warnings are not mere threats, but rather a reflection of the growing unease among our people. Have we truly considered the depth of their grievances?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
